title: Transition Fill and First Injury Fill Allowances — Prescription Insurance on File Plan Classes
content:
Two plan-class allowances of **Prescription Insurance on File** let a plan pay for a drug before its ordinary rules would: a transition fill for a new enrollee's non-formulary drug, and a first fill after a workplace injury paid before the injury claim is accepted. The figures below are the class settings; a figure of 0 means the allowance does not apply to the class.

| Plan class | Transition fill allowed | Transition fill largest days supply | Transition window (calendar days from the plan effective date) | First fill before acceptance (days supply) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit | No | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Medicare Part D Standard Plan | Yes | 30 | 90 | 0 |
| Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan | Yes | 30 | 90 | 0 |
| Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Plan | Yes | 30 | 90 | 0 |
| Commercial High-Deductible Health Plan | No | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Commercial Copay Plan | No | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit | No | 0 | 0 | 7 |

## What the columns mean

- **Transition fill allowed** — whether a non-formulary drug may be paid as a transition fill for a new enrollee.
- **Transition fill largest days supply** — the largest days supply of a transition fill.
- **Transition window** — calendar days from the plan effective date during which transition fills are paid.
- **First fill before acceptance** — days supply paid on a first fill before the injury claim is accepted; 0 means not applicable.

## At a glance

- The three Medicare classes are the only classes that pay transition fills, each up to 30 days supply within 90 calendar days of the plan effective date.
- The Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit is the only class with a first fill before acceptance, of up to 7 days supply.
- The Medicaid class and the two commercial classes carry neither allowance.
